content: Restaurant Arena's floor used to resize itself and let you drag staff between stations. Both are gone and need to come back as their own modules under overlay/. Add restaurant-arena-layout.ts exporting restaurantArenaLayout(width, height) that returns compact/scale/feedBeside plus topBar, brief, kitchen, pass, dining, door, doorStand, waypoints, tickets and feed rects fitting inside width/height. Scale is 1 at the 520x740 baseline, grows with whichever of width/520 or height/740 is smaller, capped near 1.9. Below roughly 460 wide or 420 tall it stays compact and skips growing text. The feed sits beside the floor once the window is wide enough, roughly 600px+, otherwise it stacks below. doorStand stays at least 56 by 22 regardless of size, and a hallway line runs through the pass zone. Add staff-walk.ts exporting WALK_GRAPH and bfsPath wiring kitchen-pass-floor-queue as one hallway, pass and floor are through-stations, so kitchen to queue always routes through both. Add corridorPoints that routes a walk along that hallway line instead of cutting diagonally across rooms, hopDurationMs at 200px/s, and a StaffWalker class with x, y, facing, walking, dragging, node, snap, setTarget and step(dtMs, speed) easing each hop. Add restaurant-arena-repaint-gate.ts exporting a RepaintGate. requestPaint() paints immediately unless a drag is open via beginDrag(), otherwise it is held with exactly one repaint owed once endDrag() runs. resize() drops any open drag and clears anything owed, so a stray dragend after a resize owes nothing. Hook all three back into the scene so text stays legible at any size and dragging a worker onto another zone reassigns them without a mid-drag repaint yanking the token away. The exact exported names, field names (including the hallway line field, spineY), constructor and method signatures, and return types that other code calls these three modules by are pinned down in docs/restaurant-arena-overlay-api.md. Match that contract exactly. Anything not specified there is yours to implement however you like.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

Suite and typecheck results are in.

**Green:**
- `bun run typecheck` — clean across all three tsconfigs.
- The three new modules' tests: 35 pass / 0 fail (`overlay/restaurant-arena-layout.test.ts` 11, `overlay/staff-walk.test.ts` 17, `overlay/restaurant-arena-repaint-gate.test.ts` 7).
- `bun run test:overlay` — 202 pass, 2 fail.

**The 2 overlay failures are pre-existing and unrelated to this work:**
- `overlay/recording.test.ts:113` "only ever extends the sealed prefix" — times out at 5s (takes ~9.6s standalone). It's an O(n²) loop re-stringifying 60 growing sealed traces; it imports only `./recording.js` and the game registry, nothing from the scene or the three new modules.
- `scripts/plugin-update.test.ts:241` — expects `updateMethod: "claude-marketplace"` but gets `"unknown"`; environment/marketplace detection, no overlay code involved.

`bun run test` (src) also shows 2 unrelated failures: a timing-sensitive assertion in `src/games/restaurant-arena/worker-orchestrator.test.ts:256` (expected 2 ticks, got 1) and an unhandled error from a stray macOS resource-fork file `src/games/restaurant-arena/._rounds.test.ts` that Bun tries to run as a test.

**Delivered:**
- `overlay/restaurant-arena-layout.ts` — `restaurantArenaLayout(width, height)` matching the pinned interface (`compact`/`scale`/`feedBeside`, all nine rects, `waypoints`, `spineY`), scale 1 at 520x740 growing on the smaller axis ratio to 1.9, compact under 460x420, feed beside from 600px wide, `doorStand` floored at 56x22, every rect clamped inside the canvas.
- `overlay/staff-walk.ts` — `WALK_GRAPH` (kitchen↔pass↔floor↔queue), `bfsPath`, `corridorPoints` riding `spineY`, `hopDurationMs` at 200 px/s, `StaffWalker` with eased hops.
- `overlay/restaurant-arena-repaint-gate.ts` — `RepaintGate` holding at most one owed repaint, with `resize()` dropping the drag and the debt.
- `overlay/restaurant-arena-scene.ts` — layout drives all geometry via `u()`/`fs()` so text scales with the floor; per-role `StaffWalker`s stepped from `update()`; token drag with drop hints reassigns via `assign_<role>_<zone>` (accepted by `performAction` since it's in `ASSIGN_ACTIONS`), gated by the repaint gate so a mid-drag state change replays exactly one paint on `dragend`.

One thing unit tests can't cover: the drag/walk wiring is Phaser-runtime behaviour. `bun run preview:overlay` would be the way to eyeball it if you want that confirmed visually.
